findings.detail: All-PIK debt rows with N/A spread still disclose numeric PIK rates in the Interest Rate column and should not be stored with blank interest_rate.
The same N/A-spread plus numeric PIK-rate pattern recurs on positive fair-value PPV Intermediate rows contributing to the missing-rate residual.
Subordinated debt rows for Denali Bidco disclose PIK rates despite N/A spread, confirming the issue is extraction of the rate cell rather than legitimate no-rate debt.

rationale: C01 is an aggregate interest-rate coverage failure: only 67.5% of 791 debt rows have rates, below the 0.8 threshold, with a 31.002 million FV residual. Raw SOI rows show a localized pattern where spread is N/A but the Interest Rate column contains numeric PIK rates on positive fair-value debt rows, e.g. Any Hour 13.00% PIK, PPV Intermediate 14.75% PIK, and Denali Bidco 11.20% PIK. These are not source-blank N/A(6) rows; the stored missing interest_rate is an extraction gap.
